newsitem.title: UK: Giving blood lowers risk of heart attack - study.
newsitem.headline: Giving blood lowers risk of heart attack - study.

text.p: Men who give blood seem to be at lower risk of heart attacks than those who do not, Finnish researchers said on Friday.
The report in the British Medical Journal said this could be because donating blood lowers the iron level, which is linked with heart attack risk.
Jukka Salonen and colleagues at the University of Kuopio in Finland checked 2,600 men who were taking part in a heart disease study.

They found that 153 of the participants gave blood in the two years before their first examination. Of them only one, or less than one percent, had a heart attack compared to 226 or 9.8 percent of the non-donors.
Filtering out other possible factors such as medical history and health barely changed the percentages, they said.
"This is the first study to report a reduced risk of coronary events in male blood donors," they wrote.

"The mechanism through which donating blood reduces the risk of coronary events could be the depletion of body iron stores," they added. Some studies indicate that blood loss through menstruation could be one reason why women have fewer heart attacks than men.
High iron levels also seem to affect the process during which fats oxidise and harden on the walls of arteries, which can lead to heart attacks and heart disease.

"However, voluntary blood donors seem to be generally more health-conscious and more healthy than those who do not donate blood," they added, saying this could affect who took part in the study. They concluded that more research was needed.
